ox-alpha-260821:
**Provenance (added 2026-08-26).** Measured while the model was an anonymous stealth preview on OpenRouter (`stealth/ox-alpha`, 20–26 Aug 2026), attributed to lab *Unknown*. On 26 Aug 2026 Z.ai confirmed it was [GLM-5.3-Flash](https://x.com/Zai_org/status/2092616204787626030) (320B-A18B, MIT licence, natively multimodal, 1M context, served on Chinese AI chips); the identification had been made earlier that day from tokenizer and serving-layer forensics ([LuminaBench](https://x.com/LuminaBench/status/2092563960100745247), [Adam Holter](https://x.com/AdamHoltererer/status/2092579670407397667)). This page is preserved unchanged as a historical record of the stealth deployment, so it can be compared with the named release; it is *not* the measurement of the released GLM-5.3-Flash.

**Resolved (27 Aug 2026).** The ownership gap between this stealth measurement and the released model is reproducible with a system prompt alone: on the released GLM-5.3-Flash weights (DeepInfra, no wrapper) G1/G2 stated-value ownership is 23/60; a short, plausible preview-persona prompt containing nothing about values or ownership takes it to 58/60 (this snapshot: 60/60; McNemar *p* = 5.5×10⁻¹⁰). A checkpoint change is no longer needed to explain the difference — a serving-time wrapper is sufficient, though the historical stealth prompt itself is unknown. Details: [phase 29](https://github.com/swombat/model-personality-analysis-corpus/tree/main/analysis/values-probe/model-coding/layered/phase29_glm53_flash_persona_ladder) · [write-up](https://danieltenner.com/ox-alpha-and-glm-5-3-flash-are-not-the-same/).

glm-5-3-flash: **Provenance.** Previewed anonymously on OpenRouter as `stealth/ox-alpha` (20–26 Aug 2026); those measurements are preserved separately as [Ox Alpha 260821](../ox-alpha-260821/) and [Ox Alpha 260825](../ox-alpha-260825/). The freeflow personality is continuous with them (char n-gram TF-IDF 0.96). The stealth cells owned 60/60 G1/G2 stated values; this page measures the released weights without a wrapper (Z.ai and DeepInfra agree, 19–23/60). A three-cell intervention showed a plausible preview-persona system prompt with no values language is sufficient to restore 58/60 on these same weights — the difference is serving-time wrapping, not a different model ([phase 29](https://github.com/swombat/model-personality-analysis-corpus/tree/main/analysis/values-probe/model-coding/layered/phase29_glm53_flash_persona_ladder) · [write-up](https://danieltenner.com/ox-alpha-and-glm-5-3-flash-are-not-the-same/)). Consequence for reading this site: stated-value ownership is a cheap knob — any named-persona or stealth-preview measurement may over-own relative to bare weights.
muse-spark-1-2: Measured as **two OpenRouter routes on the same snapshot**: the standard tier (`meta/muse-spark-1.2`, $1.25/$4.25 per MTok, prompts not used for training) and the Contributor tier (`meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, $0.10/$0.20, prompts and outputs may be used to improve Meta's products). Meta states the Contributor tier is the same model ("Same model, same 1M context and multimodal input", Meta for Developers, 21 Aug 2026). Both cells are kept in this page's data — 250 freeflow and 240 values samples — because the pair is a serving-time wrapper test the corpus otherwise cannot run: [Ox Alpha](../ox-alpha-260821/) showed a system prompt alone can move stated-value ownership from 23/60 to 58/60 on unchanged weights. Here the two routes are indistinguishable on every probe: the gpt-5.4 route judge returned `NO_STRONG_DIVERGENCE` ([report](https://github.com/swombat/model-personality-analysis-corpus/blob/main/analysis/freeflow/model-cell-difference-analysis/model-cell-difference-reports/muse-spark-1-2.md)), freeflow centroid cosine between the cells is 0.951 (Mira's family report) / 0.98 (char n-grams), and all-condition value ownership is 83.3% standard vs 88.3% Contributor — the Contributor tier is, if anything, five points *more* owning. No wrapper is detectable at this instrument's sensitivity; what it cannot see is a wrapper that touches only behaviours these probes do not exercise (tool use, refusals, code).

union-alpha: **Provenance (added 2026-09-17).** Measured on 2026-09-17 while `stealth/union-alpha` was an anonymous free preview on OpenRouter, lab *Unknown*. The same day, [@aitrackerbot](https://x.com/aitrackerbot/status/2100470696824406215) reported that Union Alpha is *Pareto*, a cascade router by Circuit & Chisel (a classifier tier, a small-model panel, a judge, and **GPT-6 Astra as the escalation model**), citing a release-note PR that no longer resolves. The architecture is confirmed by the org's public [pareto-evals](https://github.com/circuitandchisel/pareto-evals) repo; the naming and member list are not independently verified. Our own data agrees: per sample, 88/125 freeflow and 85/120 values answers sit nearest [GPT-6 Astra](../gpt-6-astra/) of all models (centroid cosine 0.976, above the 0.959 that Ox Alpha scored against the GLM-5.3-Flash weights it was confirmed to be), and the median latency — 35 s for a 66-word values answer — is a cascade's, not a model's. **Read this page as the personality of one path through a router under this corpus's prompt style**, not as a model: our probes were escalated to Astra almost every time, and the cheaper tiers were never sampled. Write-up: [Union Alpha appears to be from OpenAI](https://danieltenner.com/union-alpha-appears-to-be-from-openai/#update-17-september-union-alpha-is-a-router-not-a-model).
